Eight persons, Bhavna, Chetan, Gopal, Harish, Kabir, Pranav, Sameer and Yash, sit around a square table, not necessarily in the same order. Four of them sit at the four corners and the other four sit at the middle of each side. Some of them face the centre while the others face outside. 3. Bhavna sits second to the right of Harish.
4. Chetan sits second to the right of the one who sits to the immediate left of Kabir.
5. Pranav and Sameer face the same direction.
6. Both the immediate neighbours of Harish face outside.
7. Yash is not an immediate neighbour of Chetan.
8. Harish sits exactly opposite Kabir.
9. Sameer sits second to the left of Yash, who faces the centre.

Clue 1 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Bhavna second to the left of Kabir, Bhavna faces the centre and Chetan faces outside; Case 2: Bhavna 2 seats clockwise from Kabir, Bhavna faces outside and Harish faces the centre.

Clues 9, 5 and 4 then place Sameer and Chetan.
Gopal takes the only seat left.

Final arrangement, clockwise from the top-left corner: Gopal [outside] (corner), Harish [outside] (middle), Chetan [outside] (corner), Bhavna [centre] (middle), Yash [centre] (corner), Kabir [outside] (middle), Sameer [centre] (corner), Pranav [centre] (middle).

solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: Chetan is third to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

Clue 2 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Q third to the right of T and Q faces the centre; Case 2: Q third to the left of T and Q faces outside.
Clue 5 splits Case 1 into 2 cases — Case 1a: R second to the left of Q and S faces the centre; Case 1b: R opposite Q.
Clue 7 cannot be met in Case 1b, so it is rejected.
Clues 7 and 1 then place S and U.
Clue 3 splits Case 1a into 2 cases — Case 1aa: W faces the centre; Case 1ab: R faces the centre and U faces outside.
Clue 9 cannot be met in Case 1aa, so it is rejected.
Clue 9 then places the next persons.

Final arrangement, clockwise from the top-left corner: P [outside] (corner), V [outside] (middle), Q [centre] (corner), U [outside] (middle), R [centre] (corner), W [outside] (middle), S [centre] (corner), T [outside] (middle).
In "P, U", "T, Q", "W, P" and "S, U", the second person sits third to the right of the first.
In "V, S", S sits third to the left of V — so **V, S** is the odd one.
solution.shortcut: Find the relation in the first two pairs (same direction, same count), then test the rest.
solution.trap: Check direction from the first person’s own facing — a pair that is the same distance but on the other side does not belong.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true according to the given arrangement?
options: Only two persons sit between V and R
V sits to the immediate left of Q
R sits to the immediate right of W

steps: Start with clues 4, 6, 10 and 8: together they fix V, W, P and T. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Clue 2 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Q third to the right of T and Q faces the centre; Case 2: Q third to the left of T and Q faces outside.
Clue 5 splits Case 1 into 2 cases — Case 1a: R second to the left of Q and S faces the centre; Case 1b: R opposite Q.
Clue 7 cannot be met in Case 1b, so it is rejected.
Clues 7 and 1 then place S and U.
Clue 3 splits Case 1a into 2 cases — Case 1aa: W faces the centre; Case 1ab: R faces the centre and U faces outside.
Clue 9 cannot be met in Case 1aa, so it is rejected.
Clue 9 then places the next persons.

Final arrangement, clockwise from the top-left corner: P [outside] (corner), V [outside] (middle), Q [centre] (corner), U [outside] (middle), R [centre] (corner), W [outside] (middle), S [centre] (corner), T [outside] (middle).
(A) Only two persons sit between V and R — **true**.
(B) P faces the centre — false.
(C) U faces the centre — false.
(D) V sits to the immediate left of Q — false.
(E) R sits to the immediate right of W — false.
solution.shortcut: Test each statement on the final diagram, not on the clue list.
solution.trap: A statement copied from a clue with one word changed (left ↔ right, second ↔ third) looks familiar but is wrong.
